newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Burton sees more margin growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Burton sees more margin growth.

text.p: Andrew Higginson, finance director of British clothes retailer Burton Group Plc, said on Thursday he saw more scope for gross margins to improve this year although the pace of that growth would slow.
"There is still some scope for margin improvement this year, but be it at a lower pace. It will ease back somewhat from where we are at the moment," said Higginson.

Burton's gross margins for the first nine weeks of the current year to November 2 improved 1.1 percentage points. Gross margins for the year to August 31 rose 2.3 points, as it managed to move away from discounts to higher margin, own-label brands.
The gross margin improvement was also driven by changes to Burton's supply chain in the second half of the year.
Higginson described the current trading environment as better than anything seen since the early 1990's but certainly not booming.
The group reported a 7.1 percent increase in sales to 2.007 billion stg in the year ended August 31 with sales at its Debenham stores up by 6.1 percent.
Costs increased by 6.0 percent on last year. Retail profits for the year rose by 59.5 million to 161.6 million. Pretax profits increased 54 percent to 151.6 million.

Debenhams retail profits grew 20.8 million stg last year to 102.8 million and Burton plans to open a four more Debenham stores this year. Profits at Top Shop/Top Man stores more than doubled to 19.9 million stg in the year.

Burton Menswear returned to profit for the first time in three years, posting earnings of 3.3 million compared with a 4.2 million loss last year. Burton's Dorothy Perkins stores saw retail profits increase by 11.4 million to 15.5 million.
Evans stores increased retail profits 19 percent in the year to 16.3 million.
"At the moment the focus is on the core retail division where the key oppurtunities lie. Home shopping is a medium-term project which will kick in in two to three years time."

The group acquired Innovations in July, giving Burton access to the home shopping market. Racing Green, acquired in October, is also earmarked to slot a casual brand into its home shopping ambitions. Burton has a significant charge card base, with some 30 percent of its sales accounted for by five million customers using Burton's own store card. "We see home shopping as entirely complementary with retail. It will allow us to get our brands out much quicker."
